_comment: Static-analysis debt ceilings. These may only ever DECREASE.
Checkstyle, PMD and SpotBugs had never executed against this codebase before 2026-08-09 —
the audit proved it by observing that none of the three plugins had ever been downloaded to
the local repository. Turning them on produced 700 violations at once, which is far too many
to fix in one change and far too many to justify leaving ungated.
A ratchet resolves that. The gate does not demand zero; it demands 'no worse than today'.
New debt is blocked from the first run, and every fix lowers the ceiling permanently. This is
the same mechanism already used for line coverage (jacoco.minimum.coverage). It was also used
for dynamic dispatch (benchmarks/results/indy-ceiling.txt); that one was retired on
2026-08-11 because it counted invokedynamic as a proxy for Groovy, and with Groovy gone it
only counted lambdas and record accessors — it failed a build for adding a `record`. It is
now an observation. A ratchet on a metric that grows with correct work gets switched off.
Checkstyle is NOT ratcheted — its 9 violations were all unused imports and were fixed
outright, so it is a hard zero-tolerance gate.
To lower a ceiling: fix violations, run
then set the new counts here in the same commit. Raising a ceiling requires a written
justification in the commit message and CODEOWNERS approval.
_scope_2026_08_17: THE FIVE-CLASS SPOTBUGS EXCLUDE BLOCK IS GONE, AND THE FOLLOW-UP IT OWED IS DISCHARGED.
src/main/spotbugs/spotbugs-exclude.xml carried a five-class x three-pattern <Match> with no
<Method> narrowing, masking ten findings in hand-written Java. All ten are fixed and the
block is deleted rather than narrowed. Nothing about it survived: JsonFlattener and
JsonReconstructor never contributed a single finding to it and were pure collateral.
MEASURED, and two predictions were WRONG in the same direction - both gates fell further
than the analysis predicted. Stated loudly rather than quietly banked:
SpotBugs  241 -> 237.  PREDICTED 241 (no change).
The prediction was that fixing the ten could not lower the number, because 241 was the
count WITH the block and 251 the count WITHOUT it - the ten ARE the difference. That
arithmetic is right, and the number still fell by 3, because THREE findings that were
always counted inside the 241 lived inside the body of one of the deleted methods:
DE_MIGHT_IGNORE       AvroReconstructor.calculateArraySize   (the empty catch)
REC_CATCH_EXCEPTION   AvroReconstructor.calculateArraySize   (same catch)
SF_SWITCH_NO_DEFAULT  AvroReconstructor.calculateArraySize   (switch on arrayFormat)
Deleting dead code took its live findings with it. 241 - 3 = 238.
A FOURTH came off with the BL-010 constructor repair, and it is worth naming because
the gate had been reporting the bug all along at HIGH priority:
NP_NULL_ON_SOME_PATH  JsonFlattener.<init>  'Possible null pointer dereference of
config ... Dereferenced at line 224, Known null at line 223'
That is JsonFlattener.with(flattener, null) throwing NPE - the guard on 223 defeated by
the parameter read on 224. 238 - 1 = 237.
PMD       361 -> 351.  PREDICTED 353-356.
UnusedPrivateMethod       5 -> 0   the five dead methods; PMD has no per-class
exclusions and had been counting them all along
UnusedFormalParameter    40 -> 38
EmptyCatchBlock          26 -> 25
AvoidDuplicateLiterals   25 -> 24
SwitchStmtsShouldHaveDefault 2 -> 1
TWO STALE NUMBERS IN THIS FILE, corrected while re-measuring. The pmd.topRules block below
recorded AvoidLiteralsInIfCondition at 58 and EmptyCatchBlock at 25. Measured at the
PRE-CHANGE baseline they were 62 and 26. Those entries were already wrong before this work
and are now re-measured rather than carried forward.
Checkstyle unmoved at 0. Test count 2333 -> 2389 (Maven summary line, authoritative;
the surefire-XML sum reads 1840 and undercounts by 532 because @Nested classes emit a
separate report each while the outer class reports tests=0).
_scope_2026_08_11: WHY THE GROOVY REMOVAL LOWERED NOTHING HERE, measured rather than assumed.
The removal deleted 7,778 lines of Groovy, all of it under src/test. It was predicted to
move SpotBugs down. It moved nothing, and the reason is that none of the three analysers
can see test code at all:
SpotBugs    target/spotbugsXml.xml records exactly one analysed <Jar>:
target/classes. No test tree, no test classes.
So the deletion was invisible to all three by construction, and equally the ~2,700 lines of
Java the port ADDED under src/test could not have raised them either. Counts re-measured
after the removal: Checkstyle 0, PMD 361, SpotBugs 241 — all three identical to the
pre-removal ceilings, which is the expected result once the scoping above is known.
Recorded so the next reader does not spend the same hour rediscovering that a src/test
change cannot move a src/main metric.

checkstyle.note: All 9 original violations were unused imports and are fixed. Re-measured 0 on 2026-08-11 after the Groovy removal. Note this gate never saw the ported test sources: includeTestSourceDirectory is false, so the default-package AvroReconstructorTest that was moved into io.github.pierce during the port was moved for Java-tooling reasons, not because Checkstyle would have rejected it — Checkstyle was never going to look.

pmd.note: 361 -> 351 on 2026-08-17, all of it from deleting the five dead private methods the SpotBugs exclude block used to hide. This is where the ratchet actually moved: pmd-ruleset.xml pulls in category/java/bestpractices.xml whole, which contains UnusedPrivateMethod, and PMD has no per-class exclusions at all, so it had been counting all five inside its total the entire time the SpotBugs block was hiding them. Rules that fell: UnusedPrivateMethod 5 -> 0, UnusedFormalParameter 40 -> 38, EmptyCatchBlock 26 -> 25, AvoidDuplicateLiterals 25 -> 24, SwitchStmtsShouldHaveDefault 2 -> 1. The topRules figures above are re-measured; the previous entry recorded AvoidLiteralsInIfCondition as 58 and EmptyCatchBlock as 25 when the true pre-change values were 62 and 26. EARLIER: 449 -> 361 on 2026-08-10, AvoidFieldNameMatchingMethodName (88) excluded project-wide in pmd-ruleset.xml because it fires on the record-style accessor convention the language itself generates. EmptyCatchBlock (25) is still the one to attack next — it is the same swallowed-exception class the audit flagged as laundering failures into apparent successes.

spotbugs.note_2026_08_17: FOLLOW-UP DISCHARGED, block deleted, 241 -> 237. The five-class x three-pattern exclude <Match> is gone from src/main/spotbugs/spotbugs-exclude.xml and all ten findings it masked are fixed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS NOTE, both made after measuring rather than re-reading it. (1) THE COUNT. This note first said '241 -> 238' and 'THE COUNT FELL BY 3, NOT BY 0 AS PREDICTED'. Both numbers were wrong and both contradicted the ceiling stored a few lines above them in this same object. Measured with the CI command (grep -o '<BugInstance ' target/spotbugsXml.xml | wc -l): 237. The walk is 241 with the block, 251 without it, 237 after the fixes - it fell by FOUR. Three of the four lived in the body of calculateArraySize and went with the deletion (DE_MIGHT_IGNORE and REC_CATCH_EXCEPTION on its empty catch, SF_SWITCH_NO_DEFAULT on its default-less switch); the fourth is the NP_NULL_ON_SOME_PATH on the JsonFlattener constructor, repaired in the same commit and carried in its own changelog bullet. (2) THE unwrapUnion VERDICT, restated below. VERDICT ON THE FIVE DEAD PRIVATE METHODS, each established from the occurrence count of the symbol in every historical revision of its file following renames - not from reading the code and guessing: THREE WERE BORN DEAD, never called in any revision - AvroReconstructor.reconstructNestedArrayOfRecords (count 0 before cad816b, 1 in cad816b and every revision since; the live variant reconstructNestedArrayOfRecordsAtIndex was added by the SAME commit), MapFlattener.flattenSingleValue (count 1 in all 8 revisions of the file), and AvroReconstructor.unwrapUnion - which this note previously mis-filed as 'caller replaced'. unwrapUnion is born dead in the STRONGEST sense of the three: through ef625f2 the file contains FOUR occurrences of the symbol and all four are CALLS, with no declaration in any revision where a call exists; the declaration first appears at cad816b, the very commit that deleted all four calls, and never acquired a caller. The class has no superclass and the repo-wide count equals the per-file count at every revision, so it was not inherited; the file was Groovy-compiled then, so the four calls compiled and would have thrown MissingMethodException if reached. The claim 'its 3 call sites became unwrapNullable' was false twice over - there were four, and unwrapNullable's own count rose only 7 -> 8 at cad816b, so at most one site was replaced one-for-one while the branch structure was rewritten wholesale. TWO HAD CALLERS THAT A SPECIFIC COMMIT REMOVED, and in both the commit installed a named replacement at the same decision point, so nothing stopped running and no behaviour was owed restoration - AvroReconstructor.calculateArraySize (declaration at ef625f2:2018 plus one call at ef625f2:1192, which became determineArraySize, introduced by the same commit) and GAvroSchemaFlattener.isNullable(Schema), whose caller was still LIVE at 5df36e2:317 and at 1ba32af:317 and became a comment at 4a49041 - NOT at 5df36e2 as this note first said. The 4a49041 diff shows the replacement was deliberate: it adds a nullable field to SchemaNode, threads it through the constructor, and swaps the local isNullable(currentSchema) call for node.nullable. NO caller was lost, so NO corpus DEFECT is explained by any of the five, and the fidelity corpus stayed green through the change - 156 fixtures, 51/23/82 unmoved, verified rather than assumed. ONE LOSSY SUBSTITUTION IS NOW UNDOCUMENTED IN CODE and is tracked in docs/BACKLOG.md instead: determineArraySize has no BRACKET_LIST/COMMA_SEPARATED/PIPE_SEPARATED fallback where calculateArraySize did. The unwrapNullable arity-3+ gap tracked as BL-014 is NOT a lost behaviour - since unwrapUnion never executed, no arity-3+ handling was ever in service, so that entry is a never-implemented gap in the array-element path rather than a regression. CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS NOTE'S WORDING: it said 'deleting it would RAISE the ceiling, which is forbidden'. Deleting the block raises the measured COUNT to 251; the ceiling is a recorded number that only ever moves by hand. The ratchet would have rejected 251 against the 241 ceiling - that is the accurate statement, and it is why the ten had to be fixed in the same change as the deletion.
spotbugs.note_2026_08_11: SUPERSEDED by note_2026_08_17, retained for the measurement it records. UNCHANGED at 241 by the Groovy-toolchain removal, and that is itself the finding. RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY on 2026-08-11 during adversarial-review follow-up, because the review task asserted the exclude block 'named five now-deleted classes' and that SpotBugs should therefore fall. Both halves are false. (1) All five classes are present as ordinary Java: src/main/java/io/github/pierce/{AvroReconstructor,GAvroSchemaFlattener,JsonFlattener,JsonReconstructor,MapFlattener}.java. None was deleted, and src/main went Groovy-free well before this change, so nothing about porting src/test/groovy could have retired the block. Its old 'Groovy-compiled classes' label was already false when written. (2) Deleting the block and re-running spotbugs:spotbugs gives 251 <BugInstance> entries against 241 with it - 10 masked findings in hand-written Java, none a compiler artefact: UPM_UNCALLED_PRIVATE_METHOD x5, SIC_INNER_SHOULD_BE_STATIC_ANON x3, RCN_REDUNDANT_NULLCHECK_OF_NONNULL_VALUE x2. No SpotBugs ceiling reduction was earned by the Groovy removal.
spotbugs.note: 242 -> 241 on 2026-08-10: the io.github.pierce.schema package added 6 findings and now contributes 0. Four were fixed (SE_BAD_FIELD x2 - FlattenOptions declared Serializable while holding non-serializable TypeMapper and LeafInterceptor fields, so it could not serialize at all, not even with defaults; UC_USELESS_OBJECT; SE_NO_SERIALVERSIONID). Two EI_EXPOSE_REP on FlattenedField are suppressed by named method in spotbugs-exclude.xml with reasoning. Still includes EI_EXPOSE_REP on the Spark result types and SE_BAD_FIELD on NexusPiercerSparkPipeline, which corroborates the audit's finding that a non-transient SparkSession is captured into task serialization.
